opportunities.title: Small Research Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: BES members; researchers from all countries globally; projects can be conducted anywhere in the world. Not available for funding completion of an undergraduate or master's degree or projects forming part of a funded fellowship.
opportunities.summary: Funding for new and innovative ecological research of the highest international standard, with a clear ecological science focus.

opportunities.title: Long-term Research Grants

amount.raw: Up to £500 per year for a decade of data collection; first 5 years £3,500 claimable in year 1, additional £3,500 in year 6

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to all types of ecologists including conservation practitioners (e.g. reserve managers, consultants) as well as university academics; awarded to individuals not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Provides a small amount of funding each year for 10 years to enable existing short-term projects with 1-2 years of data to be funded into the long term, supporting ecological restoration, habitat creation, control of alien species and climate change anywhere in the world.

opportunities.title: Synthesis Grants

amount.raw: Up to £30,000 over two years for groups of 8-15 participants

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Main applicant must have BES membership; working groups of 8-15 individuals with diverse mix of career stages, institutions and international participation; not required for all group members to have membership.
opportunities.summary: Brings together diverse interdisciplinary groups of 8-15 individuals to focus on data analysis and synthesis, fostering collaboration and mentoring, with outputs informing decision-making by policymakers, regulators and funding agencies.

opportunities.title: Pedagogical Research and Development Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level (early years to life-long learning, formal or informal settings) and those in industry exploring teaching ideas; awarded to individuals not organisations; no geographical restrictions.
opportunities.summary: Funds research informing teaching and learning practices that improve learners' experience and promote excellence in teaching within ecology, including evidence-based practice, systematic reviews, emerging education research and dissemination of best practice.

opportunities.title: Connecting Ecologists with Other Disciplines Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations; undergraduates and masters students not eligible; awarded to individuals not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Funds a secondment/placement (up to 12 months) that immerses an ecologist in another professional world (another discipline, NGO/charity, public sector, business) to develop interdisciplinary skills and foster relationships between disciplines and sectors.

opportunities.title: Outreach and Engagement Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicant must have BES membership; open to individuals, teams and organisations across all experience levels; no restrictions on where applicants come from or where they carry out work.
opportunities.summary: Supports BES members to deliver independent outreach, public engagement and science communication activities that engage public audiences with the excitement, importance and relevance of ecological science, or enhance the skills of others to communicate ecology.

opportunities.title: Training and Travel Grants

amount.raw: Maximum £500 for in-person events; maximum £250 for virtual conferences/courses

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member and a PhD student or postgraduate researcher (PGR) registered on a postgraduate research degree programme; not open to postdocs, research staff, undergraduates or masters students; work/study at a university or research institution.
opportunities.summary: Helps PhD students and postgraduate researchers meet the costs of specialist field training courses, and travel costs associated with presenting their work at workshops and conferences. Awarded on a lottery-based system.

opportunities.title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member at any career stage; must be a citizen of and based in a Global South country; must have applied to present at the Annual Meeting; at least three years since last BES Training and Travel Grant award.
opportunities.summary: Supports researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting in the UK, covering travel from country of residence to the UK and return, plus registration, transport, food and accommodation. Awarded via lottery.
